name: external-link-little-window
description: a link another macOS app hands over opens in a Little Atrium window rather than a space window. Drives the real entry point - `open -a Atrium <url>` sends the openURLs Apple Event that -[AppController application:openURLs:] serves - because typing a URL into the address bar is a different path and would say nothing about this one. Counts WINDOWS rather than reading a log line: 'the app decided little' and 'a window exists' are different claims, and only the second is what the feature promises. The settings fixture deliberately OMITS externalLinksOpenInLittle, so this also pins the absent-key default: a profile that has never seen the row routes the same as one carrying true. Its control is external-link-space-window, which stages the same fixture with the key false and expects the count to stay at one.
chromium_flags_note: --force-renderer-accessibility is a MEASUREMENT flag, not a behaviour one. Chromium builds a renderer accessibility tree only for an assistive technology, so without it every window's AX subtree stops at the native views and the chrome route cannot be read at all - measured on 2026-08-11: urls=[] for all three windows, then chrome://atrium.top-chrome/sidebar the moment the flag was on. It changes nothing about which window type opens, and the scenario and its control both carry it, so the comparison between them does not rest on it.

actions.note: a loopback url is still EXTERNAL in Atrium's sense. ExternalLinkOpensLittleWindow takes three booleans - the setting, has_url, and is_http_or_https - and the core's decision never inspects the HOST (atrium_external_link.cc:56). 'External' here means handed over by another app through the openURLs Apple Event, which is what the open_url action sends, not 'on a remote server'. So this keeps testing external-link handling while reaching a page the probe VM can actually load. dl.localhost also hashes to the same row hue as example.com, so any tint assertion is undisturbed.
A little window builds a Browser, a controller and its chrome strip; little-window-hotkey settles for the same 2500ms for the same reason.

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: one startup window plus the little one the handed-over link opened. Before this stage openURLs had no Atrium hook at all and the URL became a tab in the existing window, leaving the count at one.

THE MEASUREMENT OF KIND: exactly one of the open windows is built around the foyer strip, which is the chrome only a little window has. The count above says a window opened; this says which kind, read off the window's own AX subtree rather than off a line saying what the app meant to open. If the handover opened an ordinary space window the count would still be two and this would be zero.
And the other window is the startup space window, still whole. Pins the pair: one of each, not two of either. A little window with a sidebar in it would not be a little window.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: external link opened a little window
assertions.desc: Which code path ran. Kept as corroboration only - the two kind assertions above are what the check rests on, because this line says what the app believes it did.
Cmd+Q still quits with a little window open
